issues.description: Default speaker mismatch between config and docstring/PR description for bulbul:v3-beta
issues.detail: The PR description and class docstring state the default speaker for bulbul:v3-beta is 'aditya', but TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS['bulbul:v3-beta'] sets default_speaker='shubh'. Users following the docs will end up with a different voice than documented. Either the config or the docstrings must be corrected before merge, and a test should pin the contract.
issues.lines: TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS bulbul:v3-beta entry vs class docstring and module docstring

issues.detail: Previously `connect_kwargs` included `input_audio_codec`. The new code removes this key entirely, so the codec set via `__init__(input_audio_codec=...)` is no longer forwarded to either streaming endpoint. This is a silent regression for any non-default audio codec (e.g., PCM/raw) and likely causes decoding errors at the API. The field is still stored in `self._input_audio_codec` but never used.

issues.description: saaras:v2.5 connect now omits language_code where previously it was sent as None
issues.detail: Old code unconditionally set `connect_kwargs['language_code'] = self._language_string` (which would be None for saaras). New code only adds the key when `_language_string is not None`. If the SDK's translate endpoint previously accepted/required this kwarg, omission changes the wire contract. Verify against the Sarvam SDK signature for `speech_to_text_translate_streaming.connect` and add a regression test.

issues.description: Pace clamping silently mutates user input instead of erroring
issues.detail: When the user supplies a pace outside the model's range, the code logs a warning and clamps. Pydantic's Field already enforces 0.3-3.0 globally, so v3-beta users passing pace=0.4 (valid by Field, invalid by model range) get silently changed to 0.5. Prefer raising ValueError to make the contract explicit, or tighten the Pydantic constraints conditionally. Silent clamping is a foot-gun for production audio configuration.

issues.description: Warning checks compare against defaults, not user intent
issues.detail: Logic like `elif params.pitch != 0.0: logger.warning(...)` warns the user only when their pitch differs from the default. A user who explicitly sets pitch=0.0 with v3-beta gets no warning; a user who leaves the default 0.0 gets no warning even though the value is conceptually still being ignored. Conversely, a user who sets pitch=0.0 on v3 thinking it does something gets no signal. Track whether the field was explicitly set (e.g., via `model_fields_set`) rather than value equality.

issues.description: InputParams Pydantic ranges don't reflect model-specific bounds
issues.detail: pace is declared `ge=0.3, le=3.0` at the Pydantic level, but bulbul:v3-beta's actual range is 0.5-2.0. Users get no validation feedback at construction time and instead see a runtime warning followed by silent clamping. Either narrow ranges contextually or document this discrepancy explicitly in the field description (current description mentions both ranges but Field still accepts the full 0.3-3.0).

issues.description: voice_id is not validated against the model's speaker list
issues.detail: The new SarvamTTSSpeakerV2/V3 enums and `speakers` tuple in TTSModelConfig exist precisely to enforce valid voices per model, yet `__init__` accepts any string for `voice_id` without checking membership. A user can pass a v2 speaker ('anushka') with model='bulbul:v3-beta' and the request will fail at API time rather than at construction. Add a `voice_id not in self._config.speakers` validation.

issues.description: MODEL_CONFIGS lookup is exact-match while existing code semantics included substring matches
issues.detail: Previous STT code used `'saaras' in model.lower()` substrings, which would have accepted variants like 'saaras:v3-beta-xyz'. New `model not in MODEL_CONFIGS` raises for any unknown variant. This is arguably more correct but is a hard backward-incompatible change: any caller using an undocumented-but-working model string will break on upgrade. Worth a CHANGELOG/migration note and possibly a deprecation cycle.

issues.description: Docstring typo retained: `model="bulbul:v3,` missing closing quote
issues.detail: The example in the SarvamHttpTTSService docstring still shows `model="bulbul:v3,` (missing closing quote and stale model id) in the diff context surrounding the new v3 example. Verify the original/new docstring doesn't carry this typo into shipping docs.

issues.description: get_speakers_for_model silently falls back to v2 for unknown models
issues.detail: `get_speakers_for_model('bulbul:v99')` returns the v2 speaker list without warning. Given that the rest of the module raises ValueError on unknown models, this helper is inconsistent. Either raise or log a warning so callers don't silently get wrong speaker lists.

issues.description: Mode literal duplication between Pydantic Literal and runtime config
issues.detail: The five mode strings ('transcribe', 'translate', 'verbatim', 'translit', 'codemix') are declared in the `InputParams.mode` Literal but only `default_mode` is referenced in `MODEL_CONFIGS`. If Sarvam adds a new mode for v3, two places must be updated. Consider hoisting the allowed modes per-model into the config (e.g., `allowed_modes: frozenset`) and deriving the Literal/runtime validation from one source.

issues.description: set_prompt no-op behavior is silent when model doesn't support prompts and prompt is None
issues.detail: When called with prompt=None on a saarika model, the method returns silently. This is intentional ('no-op') but could mask misconfiguration in calling code that expected a state change. Consider a debug-level log so operators can see the no-op in traces.

issues.description: Enums defined but not enforced anywhere
issues.detail: SarvamTTSModel, SarvamTTSSpeakerV2, and SarvamTTSSpeakerV3 enums are added but `model`/`voice_id` parameters are typed as `str`. The enums act only as documentation and as a source for the speakers tuple. Either accept `Union[str, SarvamTTSModel]` in __init__ and coerce, or note in docs that the enums are advisory.

dissents.topic: Pace clamping vs. raising on out-of-range input

positions.position: Clamping with a warning keeps streaming pipelines running and is forgiving for production callers who may construct configs from upstream user input.

Silent clamping violates the principle of least surprise and lets bugs propagate. Raise ValueError so misconfiguration is caught at construction time, identical to how unsupported model names are handled.

dissents.topic: Backward compatibility of strict model whitelist

positions.position: A hard whitelist via MODEL_CONFIGS is correct: the previous substring matching was a smell that allowed unsupported variants to slip through.
Any user passing an undocumented variant (e.g., the literal 'bulbul:v3' from the old example docstring) now hard-fails on upgrade. Needs a deprecation window or at least a prominent CHANGELOG entry.

dissents.topic: Default speaker for bulbul:v3-beta (aditya vs shubh)

positions.position: PR description and docstrings explicitly state 'aditya' as default; the code config is the bug — set default_speaker='aditya'.
If 'shubh' is the intended default for product reasons, fix the docs to match. Either way the divergence must be resolved before merge.

dissents.topic: Whether to validate voice_id against per-model speaker enums

positions.position: The enums and speakers tuples already encode the constraint; not using them for validation is dead structure. Validate at construction.
Sarvam may add speakers between SDK releases; a strict whitelist will force lockstep upgrades. Prefer a warning rather than a hard failure.

review.summary: The refactor to data-driven MODEL_CONFIGS / TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS is a clear improvement over substring-matched branching and the documentation is materially better. However, the PR has at least two blocking issues: (1) `input_audio_codec` is silently dropped from STT `_connect` kwargs, which is a regression for any non-default codec; (2) the bulbul:v3-beta default speaker is 'shubh' in code but documented as 'aditya' in both the PR description and class docstring. Several P1 quality concerns remain: pace is silently clamped rather than rejected, "ignored parameter" warnings compare against default values instead of explicit-set state, voice_id is not validated against the per-model enums that were just introduced, and the Pydantic ranges don't reflect per-model bounds. Resolve the codec regression and the speaker default discrepancy before merge; address the validation/warning semantics in a follow-up if needed.
